answer:
You can re-run only the ERROR results in two ways, both documented in the promptfoo docs.

**Option 1: Retry errors from the latest eval.** Run `promptfoo eval --retry-errors`. The docs say: "The retry errors feature automatically finds ERROR results from the latest eval and re-runs only those test cases. This is useful when evals fail due to temporary network issues, rate limits, or API errors." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]. Note that it "Cannot be used together with `--resume` or `--no-write` flags." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]

**Option 2: Retry errors from a specific eval.** Run `promptfoo retry <evalId>`, for example `promptfoo retry eval-abc123`. The docs say this "finds test cases that resulted in errors (e.g., from network issues, rate limits, or API failures) and re-runs only those test cases. The results are updated in place in the original eval." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]

**Safety:** For both, the docs say that if the retry fails, "your original ERROR results are preserved," and "Old ERROR results are only removed after the retry succeeds." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md] So you can run the command again if it fails.

**Which to use:** The docs say that "Unlike `--filter-errors-only` which creates a new eval, `promptfoo retry` updates the original eval in place. Use `retry` when you want to fix errors in an existing eval without creating duplicates." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]
